Mortadelo y Filemon (1988)(Dro Soft)(es)
notes: Mortadelo y Filemon: block 7 loads C9h over FC8Eh, where the stub case keeps T0's slot, and block 5 writes the mapper port of page 2 with OUT (0FEh),A, which a cassette machine ignores. FC8Eh's byte becomes T0's slot, the OUT two NOPs, and each block's XOR check byte changes with them.

title: Lady Safary (1988)(OMK Software)(es)
notes: Lady Safary: its slot code jumps to its copy in page 1, at 4042h, before it makes the copy, when slot 1 or 2 has RAM there; the jumps go to the code at 9042h that makes the copy.

title: Ship (1989)(Eurosoft)(es)
notes: Ship: its copy from 8500h to 8100h overwrites its own LDIR with bytes the file never loads; the copy stops before its own code, at 5F41h bytes.

title: M-Droid (19xx)(Blue Ribbon Software)
notes: M-Droid: it calls FFE9h, above the hooks, which neither it nor the BIOS writes; the call becomes three NOPs, as it returns on a cassette machine.

title: Chuck Yeager's Advanced Flight Trainer (1989)(Dro Soft)
notes: Chuck Yeager's Advanced Flight Trainer: its loader copies 200h bytes of its code to FACCh, over FC8Eh, where the stub case keeps T0's slot, from past the end of its block; the copy stops at 1C2h bytes, before FC8Eh, which holds all of the loader's code.

title: Gemini Wing (1989)(Virgin Mastertronic)(Side A)
notes: Gemini Wing, the dump with a loading screen: the same loader as Chuck Yeager's, and the same change.

title: BMX Simulator (1987)(Codemasters)
notes: BMX Simulator: when page 3's slot is expanded, its loader sets only the subslot register for pages 0 and 1, and copies its code into page 0, over T0; its test of EXPTBL's byte becomes two NOPs, so that it puts page 3's slot in pages 0 and 1, which the T case keeps away from T0.

title: Bestial Warrior (1989)(Dinamic Software)(es)
notes: Bestial Warrior: its slot module, which runs from page 3, puts page 3 in the slot of page 0 to set that slot's subslot register when the slot is expanded, and takes its own code away. Page 0 holds T0 in the Carnivore2's expanded slot 1, where a cassette machine holds the BIOS ROM in slot 0. The module's test of EXPTBL's expanded bit becomes AND 00h, and the entry picks R, whose T0 is out of the way of the game's search for RAM for page 0, from slot 3 down.

title: Engesoft MSXK-06 - Lado B
notes: Spelunker (Engesoft's tape): each part takes the slots for its copy of the ROM from the slot register, and expects F0h, the slots of BASIC on a cassette machine with its RAM in slot 3; any other value sends the copy to slot 2. Under CASGO page 0 holds T0, so the value differs; the test's JR Z becomes JR, so that each part copies into slot 3, the internal RAM.

title: SuperMSX18-LatoA
notes: Super MSX 18: the code that starts TIDDLE's BASIC program, which it BLOADs over the program area, writes the first line's link to 0801h instead of 8001h. A cassette machine has ROM there; CASGO has T0, whose BIOS copy the write breaks. The address becomes 8001h.

title: Rocky (1985)(Dinamic Software)(es)
notes: Rocky, the modified dump: the end of its blocks 9 and 11 puts slot 3 in every page before it copies 467Fh bytes to 0300h, where the other dump copies them into the ROM; in I the copy lands on T0. Those bytes become the other dump's. The entry matches both dumps, and the old bytes only this one.

title: Narco Police (1990)(Dinamic Software)(Side A)
notes: Narco Police, the dump with another version of the stub loader: its stub takes the slots for the tape calls as IN D,(C) / LD A,D / AND 0FCh / LD E,A, which puts the BIOS ROM in page 0, and no rule finds it. AND 0FCh becomes OR with T0's slot, as the stub case does for IN A,(0A8h) / LD H,A / AND 0FCh / LD L,A.

title: Aackobase II (1985)(Aackosoft)(nl)
notes: Aackobase II: its block PROTSL searches the slots for RAM from 84h, slot 0-1, up, and its probe of slot 1-1 leaves slot 1's subslot register selecting subslot 1 for page 0, which takes T0, in the mapper's subslot, out of page 0 in R. The search starts at 87h, slot 3, which it takes for RAM on a cassette machine too. The game then writes its RAM in every page of slot 3, so the entry picks R, whose T0 is out of the way, and the plain case, whose loader the BASIC case's changes break.

title: SUPER05A
notes: Gino e Pino, the first program of Super MSX 5: its loader searches the slots for RAM from 80h up, finds the internal RAM first, puts it in page 0 and loads 42 KB there, over T0 in I. The search starts at 88h, which skips subslots 0 and 1 and finds the mapper on a machine whose mapper is in subslot 2, as the Carnivore2's is, or in a slot that is not expanded.
